open_points.subject: Forbidden fields on surface requests
open_points.text: “an unknown field ... is refused” as `invalid_request`; but “A request that supplies one of these identities is refused” and “A proposal that states its own effect class is refused”
open_points.question: Are caller-supplied computed identities, binding effect classes and binding key fields unknown schema fields yielding `invalid_request`, or recognized forbidden fields yielding `refused`?
options: Exclude them from request schemas and return `invalid_request`
Include them as forbidden fields and return `refused`
open_points.default_guess: Exclude them from the fixed request schemas and return `invalid_request`.

open_points.subject: Authored trial cases containing files
open_points.text: “add_trial_case takes a contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs” and “A check is given a file as facts ... never bytes”
open_points.question: How does an authored trial case supply the bytes that must become a new file fixture: as bytes in this request, as a reference to an existing StoredValue, or through another operation?
options: Carry new fixture bytes in `add_trial_case`
Reference an existing file StoredValue
Add a separate fixture-ingestion operation
open_points.default_guess: Carry the fixture bytes in `add_trial_case`; surface passes bytes plus computed facts to `functions`, which publishes them before recording the case.

open_points.subject: TrialCase expected outputs
open_points.text: “optional expected outputs” and “if the case states expected outputs, every output's digest equals the expected one”
open_points.question: When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it contain only a subset whose members are compared?
options: Absent or an exact complete output-port map
A partial map is allowed and only named outputs are compared
open_points.default_guess: Require either absence or an exact complete output-port map.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity
open_points.text: M22 says “Identity: value” and “equal facts are the same spooled file”; State 5 says “A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)” and omits digest, size, media type and disclosure class from `read_spooled_file` identity
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile identified by all M22 meaning facts or solely by `(run_id, producer_node_id, map_index, attempt_number, producer_port, list_index)`?
options: Producing-position key only
All M22 facts
A separate minted identifier
open_points.default_guess: Use the producing-position key only, treating the remaining facts as attributes of the uniquely keyed record.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: With no operation name or proposed ports supplied at startup, which A08 rule 5 checks are applied, which capability entries are examined, and in what order if several entries are invalid?
options: Check only service-level JSON, service identity, instance and required-header facts needed by startup
Validate every capability entry in a defined capability order
Check only the selected instance and ignore capability entries
open_points.default_guess: Check only the service-level and selected-instance facts needed to detect credential-header collisions; leave operation-specific checks to proposal and send.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox
open_points.question: What exact code, inputs, ports, resource bounds and expected result constitute the startup probe, and which non-success outcomes produce which start reason?
options: A release-fixed probe fixture with an exact expected output
Any minimal process that starts and exits successfully
A suite probing isolation, traps and resource enforcement
open_points.default_guess: Use one release-fixed minimal function, fixed empty input and output contracts, fixed bounds, and require its exact expected output.

open_points.subject: Multipart request construction
open_points.text: “the boundary ... [is] the kernel's framing ... not a difference” and “equal parts give equal descriptions”
open_points.question: How are multipart boundaries selected and collision-checked, and what exact delimiter, CRLF and closing-boundary serialization is sent on the wire?
options: Delegate framing to the pinned HTTP library
Use a deterministic content-derived boundary and fixed serialization
Generate a fresh collision-checked boundary with fixed serialization
open_points.default_guess: Use a fresh collision-checked boundary and one explicitly fixed RFC-compliant serialization; continue excluding the boundary from the approval digest.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input representation
open_points.text: The operation takes “One JSON value” but must refuse “a duplicate key”; surface “turns every JSON text a request carries ... into its canonical form”
open_points.question: Does `canonical_bytes` receive raw JSON text or a parsed representation that preserves duplicate-member detection, since an ordinary parsed JSON value has already lost duplicate keys?
options: Receive raw JSON text and parse with duplicate rejection
Receive a duplicate-preserving parse tree
Require the surface decoder to reject duplicates before passing an ordinary value
open_points.default_guess: Require the surface decoder to reject duplicate members and non-finite numbers, then pass the parsed value to `canonical_bytes`.

open_points.subject: Manifest source and revision access
open_points.text: “manifest_location, manifest_revision: where the platform manifest is read and the repository revision it is read at” and “reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at the configured revision”
open_points.question: What repository mechanism resolves `manifest_revision`, whether it must be an immutable revision, and how the file is read from that revision are not fixed.
options: Read a Git object at an exact commit
Treat `manifest_location` as an already materialized immutable snapshot and use revision only as metadata
Use a platform-provided revisioned manifest reader
open_points.default_guess: Treat the location as a Git repository and require an exact commit identifier, reading the service file directly from that commit without changing a worktree.

open_points.subject: Agent masking of failure_detail
open_points.text: “a classified `failure_detail` [is returned] only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: Is the reported length UTF-8 byte length, Unicode scalar count, or another measure, and is it measured before or after truncation to `failure_detail_bytes_max`?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the stored truncated detail
Unicode characters of the stored truncated detail
Original pre-truncation UTF-8 byte length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already truncated failure detail.
